core_obligations: Reduce to a Tor computation (proof lines 3392-3405): the author tensors the given acyclic complex with an arbitrary module and uses K-flatness to keep acyclicity, so that the relevant sequences remain exact after tensoring.

Compute the cycles (proof lines 3405-3415): the resulting exactness identifies the cycles of the complex with the cycles of the tensored complex, and the Tor criterion for flatness applies, which shows that the module of cycles is flat.
proof_roadmap: Tensor the complex with an arbitrary module and use K-flatness to preserve acyclicity.
Read off the cycles of the tensored complex and compare with the tensor product of the cycles.
Apply the Tor criterion to conclude flatness of the cycles.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the cycles of a K-flat acyclic complex with flat terms are a flat module (statement lines 3384-3390). The proof tensors the complex with an arbitrary module, keeping acyclicity by K-flatness (proof lines 3392-3405), and then compares the cycles of the tensored complex with the tensor product of the cycles, which by the Tor criterion gives flatness (proof lines 3405-3415). The non-formal content is the identification of the cycles after tensoring. The claim is H2: one comparison plus one criterion.
